html:
The Ghaznavids were a Turkic Muslim dynasty that ruled from Ghazni, in today's Afghanistan, from 977 to 1186. At their height they held eastern Iran, Afghanistan, much of Central Asia and the Punjab.

The dynasty began with Sebüktigin, a Turkic slave soldier in the service of the Samanids, who took over Ghazni in 977. His son Mahmud, who ruled from 998 to 1030, made it an empire:

  • He raided northern India again and again, carrying off great treasure, and in 1025 sacked the temple of Somnath.
  • His court drew scholars and poets. Ferdowsi finished the Shahnameh, the Persian national epic, in his reign, and al-Biruni wrote his great study of India.

Mahmud's son lost Khorasan to the Seljuks at the Battle of Dandanaqan in 1040. The later Ghaznavids held on in Afghanistan and the Punjab, with Lahore as a second capital. The Ghurids burned Ghazni in the 1150s and took Lahore in 1186, ending the dynasty. The Ghurids' push into India led to the Delhi Sultanate.
